rules.statement: Default service registrations must never silently generate signing keys or seed key/secret stores; key material must come from operator-configured or persisted sources.
rules.why: Auto-generated default keys regenerate on restart (invalidating issued tokens), differ across instances (breaking validation), and hide a security-critical key provenance and lifecycle decision that operators must own.
rules.check: Look for default `Add*` registration methods or default providers that create RSA/EC/symmetric keys, self-signed certificates, or in-memory seeded secret stores without an explicit caller opt-in.

rules.statement: Provide ephemeral, in-memory development signing keys only through a separate, explicitly and clearly named opt-in extension method (e.g. `AddEphemeralDeveloperKeys()`) that development and test hosts call on purpose, and never persist those ephemeral keys.
rules.why: An explicit, discoverable opt-in keeps the server safe by default while still making dev/test environments runnable with one deliberate call; ephemeral keys are fine for development but must not be used in production.
rules.check: Flag development key conveniences that are applied by default, hidden behind generic names, enabled implicitly by environment detection inside library defaults, or that write generated keys to persistent storage.

rules.statement: Make create-if-missing persistence paths idempotent under concurrency, using an idempotent upsert or retry-on-conflict, not a check-then-insert that can race.
rules.why: When two first requests create the same row at the same time, a check-then-insert produces a duplicate-key failure.
rules.check: Look for code that queries whether a row exists and then inserts it, with no unique-constraint conflict handling, upsert, or retry.
